turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms. [Name]. I'm Dr. [Name], the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go over a few things to make sure we're all set for your laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Is that okay with you?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, doctor. Thank you lah.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great. Can you tell me a bit about why you're having this surgery? What symptoms have you been experiencing?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Sure. I've been having this sharp pain on the right side of my belly, especially after eating. The doctor said it's gallstones, and they want to remove the gallbladder laparoscopically.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Understood. Now, let's go through your medications. You're currently on amlodipine, metoprolol, atorvastatin, omeprazole, and you've stopped aspirin. Is that correct?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, doctor. I take all those except the aspirin, which I stopped a week ago as instructed.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. Now, regarding allergies—your records say 'no known allergies,' but I always like to confirm directly. Do you have any allergies to medications, including antibiotics like penicillin?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Oh, actually, yes. When I was younger, I took penicillin for a infection and got a bad rash all over. So I think I'm allergic to that.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. It's important we update your records to reflect your penicillin allergy. Have you had any other reactions to medications?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, just that one time with penicillin. Other antibiotics seem fine.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Excellent. Have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight? We need to ensure you're NPO for surgery.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, doctor. I had water until 6 AM but nothing else. My wife made sure I followed the instructions.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Perfect. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? Any complications like nausea, breathing issues, or high blood pressure during recovery?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I had my appendix out when I was a teenager. The anesthesia was fine then—no problems at all.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great. Lastly, how are you managing with daily activities? Any shortness of breath, chest pain, or difficulty mobilizing due to your weight or other conditions?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I can walk and do my usual things, but sometimes I get a bit breathless if I rush. My blood pressure has been controlled with the meds, and I take omeprazole for the acid reflux.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for all that information. We'll proceed with general anesthesia and rapid sequence induction as planned. Your penicillin allergy will be clearly documented. Any questions for me before we head to the operating room?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, doctor. Just want to make sure stopping the aspirin was the right call.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Absolutely. Stopping it a week prior reduces bleeding risk during surgery. We'll manage your pain post-op with other medications. All set then?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, thank you. I'm ready.
